resources.string: Slide the tiles back into order

Slide the numbered tiles into the gap until they read in order, left to right and top to bottom, with the gap in the bottom-right corner.\n\nTap a tile in the same row or column as the gap: every tile between it and the gap slides along.
Tapping a square flips a pattern of squares around it, drawn in small inside the square. Switch every square off.
Shift rows and columns to sort the tiles

Put the tiles back in order, left to right and top to bottom.\n\nThe arrows around the edge shift a whole row or column by one square: the tile pushed off one side comes back on the other. You can also drag a row or column along.
Turn blocks of tiles to sort the grid

Put the tiles back in order, left to right and top to bottom. Each tile wears the colour of the row it belongs to.\n\nTap to turn the block under your finger a quarter turn clockwise; long-press to turn it the other way.
Jump the pegs until only one is left

A peg jumps over a neighbouring peg, horizontally or vertically, into the empty hole just behind it; the jumped peg is removed. Finish with a single peg.\n\nTap a peg to pick it up, then tap where it should land, or drag it there.
Move the points until no lines cross
Drag the points around until no line crosses another. Lines that still cross are drawn in red.
Fill the grid with one colour

The patch in the top-left corner takes the colour you choose and swallows every neighbouring square of that colour. Turn the whole grid into a single colour before running out of moves.\n\nTap a colour below the grid, or any square of that colour.
Clear the grid group by group

Remove groups of two or more touching squares of the same colour. Squares above fall down and empty columns close up to the left. Clear the whole grid. A group of n squares scores (n − 2)².\n\nTap a group to select it and see its score, tap it again to remove it.

Find the hidden row of colours. After each guess, a filled pin means a right colour in the right place, a hollow pin a right colour in the wrong place.\n\nTap a colour to fill the circled slot; tap a slot to choose it, tap it again to empty it. The tick submits the guess.
Build the skyline from what each side can see

Each row and each column holds every height from 1 to the grid size exactly once. A number outside the grid says how many towers you can see from there, taller towers hiding shorter ones behind them.\n\nTap a square, then a number below. The pencil switches to small notes.
A Latin square with greater-than signs

Each row and each column holds every number from 1 to the grid size exactly once. Every sign between two squares must hold: its point faces the smaller number.\n\nTap a square, then a number below. The pencil switches to small notes.
A Latin square in arithmetic cages

Each row and each column holds every number from 1 to the grid size exactly once. The numbers in each outlined cage must produce its target with the operation shown; for − and ÷, take the larger number first.\n\nTap a square, then a number below. The pencil switches to small notes.
Two colours, balanced, never three in a row

Fill the grid with two colours. Every row and every column holds as many squares of each colour, and three squares in a row, across or down, are never the same colour.\n\nTap to cycle a square through the colours; long-press to cycle backwards. Squares marked with a dot are given.
Place bulbs to light every square

Place bulbs so that every white square is lit. A bulb lights its row and column up to the nearest wall. Two bulbs must never shine on each other, and a numbered wall touches exactly that many bulbs.\n\nTap to place or remove a bulb; long-press to mark a square that holds no bulb.
Paint the hidden picture from the clues

Fill in squares so that each row and column shows the blocks listed beside it, in that order, with at least one gap between blocks.

The chips below choose what a tap does: fill or cross out. Long-press does the other. Drag to apply it along a row or column. With Help on, a number is struck out as soon as its block fills exactly the right squares.

Pictures: hand-drawn grids, each one unlocking the next, revealed in colour once solved. The Gallery shows the finished ones and lets you play any of them again.
Divide the grid into rectangles. Each rectangle contains exactly one number, equal to its area.\n\nDrag from one corner square to the opposite one to draw a rectangle. Tap a rectangle to erase it.

A complete set of dominoes was laid out to fill the grid, then the outlines were erased. Find where each domino lies: every pair of numbers appears exactly once.\n\nTap the border between two squares, or drag from one to the other, to place a domino. Tap it again to remove it.

Place one moon beside each planet (left, right, above or below), one moon per planet. Two moons never touch, not even diagonally. The numbers count the moons in each row and column.\n\nTap a square to place a moon; long-press to mark it as empty space.
Black out repeats, keep the rest joined

Black out squares so that no number appears twice in a row or column among the squares left white. Black squares never touch side by side, and all the white squares stay joined in one piece.\n\nTap to black out a square; long-press to circle one you are sure stays white.
Reveal the picture from its numbers

Each number counts the black squares in the three-by-three block centred on it, itself included. Find which squares are black.

Tap to black out a square; long-press to mark it white.

Pictures: the same drawings as in Logimage, each one unlocking the next, revealed in colour once solved. The Gallery chip shows them.
Black out squares so each number sees its count

Black out squares so that each number sees exactly that many white squares in straight lines in the four directions, itself included, up to the first black square or the edge. Black squares never touch side by side, and all the white squares stay joined in one piece.\n\nTap to black out a square; long-press to mark it white.
Follow the arrows through every square

Link every square into one path numbered from 1 to the last square, marked with a star. Each arrow points the way to the next square, which can be any distance away in that direction.\n\nDrag from a square to the one that follows it. A chain that reaches a given number numbers itself. Tap a square to undo its links.
Find the hidden nuclei with alpha particles
Colour the map with four colours

Colour every country with one of the four colours so that no two neighbouring countries share a colour. Countries with a dot are already coloured.\n\nPick a colour below, then tap the countries to paint. Long-press a country to clear it.
Grow every number into a block of its size

Fill every square with a number so that each block of touching squares holding the same number has exactly that many squares.\n\nTap a square, then a number below. Drag from a numbered square to copy its number along your path.
Fill the grid with diagonals, never a loop

Draw a diagonal in every square. A number on a corner says how many diagonals touch it, and the diagonals must never form a closed loop.\n\nTap to cycle a square through \\ and /; long-press to cycle the other way.

The network was scrambled by shifting whole rows and columns. Shift them back so that every tile is connected to the source, with no pipe leading nowhere.\n\nThe arrows around the edge shift a row or column by one; you can also drag it along.
Roll the ball to collect every gem

The ball rolls in one of eight directions and only stops on a stop square (a ring) or in front of a wall. It collects the gems it rolls over. A mine destroys it, but you can undo. Collect every gem.\n\nSwipe anywhere in the direction to roll, or tap where you want it to go.
Draw one loop around the numbers

Draw a single closed loop along the grid lines, never crossing or touching itself. A number in a square says how many of its four sides the loop uses.\n\nTap a side to draw or erase it, long-press to mark it with a cross, or drag to draw along your path.
Thread one loop through every pearl

Draw a single closed loop from square centre to square centre that passes through every pearl.
On a black pearl the loop turns, then goes straight through the next square on both sides.
On a white pearl the loop goes straight through, and turns in at least one of the two squares beside it.

Tap between two squares to link them, long-press to mark a cross, or drag to draw along your path.
Lay the railway from entrance to exit

Lay one continuous railway from the entrance on the left edge to the exit on the bottom edge. It never crosses itself and never loops. The numbers say how many squares of each row and column it runs through. Some pieces of track are already laid.\n\nTap between two squares to link them, long-press to mark a cross, or drag to lay track along your path.

The grid is covered with dominoes. Each one is either a dipole, with a + charge and a − charge, or a neutral pair. Two charges of the same sign never touch side by side: they would spark. The numbers count the + charges (top and left) and the − charges (bottom and right) of each row and column.\n\nTap a domino to turn it into + −, then − +, then neutral, then empty; long-press goes the other way.
Ghosts, vampires and zombies in a hall of mirrors

Fill every empty square with a ghost, a vampire or a zombie. A number on the edge says how many monsters you see looking in from there, your gaze bouncing off the mirrors. A vampire is only seen directly, never in a mirror; a ghost only in a mirror; a zombie always. The totals of each monster are shown above the grid.\n\nTap a square to cycle ghost, vampire, zombie, empty; long-press to cycle backwards.
Fence the grid into equal plots

Split the grid into regions that all have the size shown in the settings, by drawing walls along the grid lines. A number in a square says how many of its four sides are walls; the outer edge of the grid counts as a wall.\n\nTap a line to draw or erase a wall, long-press to mark it as open, drag to draw several at once.
Carve the sky into symmetric galaxies

Split the grid into galaxies by drawing walls along the grid lines. Each galaxy contains exactly one star, and looks the same after a half-turn around its star.\n\nTap a line to draw or erase a wall, long-press to mark it as open, drag to draw several at once. A finished galaxy takes the colour of its star.
Roll the cube to collect every colour

Roll the cube across the board. When it lands on a coloured square, the colour moves onto its bottom face; when a coloured face lands on a plain square, the colour goes back down onto the square. Colour all six faces.
Tap beside the cube or swipe to roll it. The unfolded cube under the board shows every face, including the one underneath.
